strengths: Well-motivated problem: addresses the real practical challenge that different AL strategies perform inconsistently across datasets, models, and AL cycles
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 6 image datasets, 3 foundation models, 20 AL cycles with 10 trials; strong empirical results (85% win rate vs. BAIT, 100% vs. SelectAL)
Solid theoretical analysis with three theorems providing formal grounding for value preservation, exponential filtering of uninformative instances, and concentration toward high-value pools
Practical utility: progressive filtering works as a standalone preprocessing step improving diverse individual strategies (+0.7% to +5.4%)
Clear, intuitive methodology that is simple to implement and ecosystem-friendly (works with existing strategies)
Extensive ablation studies examining hyperparameter sensitivity (R, α, J) and demonstrating robustness across configurations
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: progressive filtering is a straightforward multi-round extension of existing single-step filtering methods (DropQuery, AlfaMix); core idea of using unions is intuitive but not particularly novel

Critical dependence on strategy ensemble composition: effectiveness depends heavily on complementary, well-performing strategies with no principled guidance for selection; acknowledged failure case (Dopanim+CLIP) when majority of strategies underperform
Problematic hyperparameter tuning: α, R, J selected on CIFAR-10 but CIFAR-10 excluded from main results, creating potential bias; no cross-dataset validation of hyperparameters
Insufficient failure analysis: Dopanim+CLIP degradation mentioned briefly but not deeply investigated; lacks analysis of what dataset/model/strategy properties predict failure modes

Theoretical limitations: bounds in Theorems 1-2 are loose and don't directly explain practical performance gains; ϵ-uninformative definition is somewhat arbitrary with no practical guidance on setting ϵ

Incomplete computational analysis: complexity stated but no wall-clock time comparisons provided; parallelization benefits mentioned but not empirically validated; memory overhead during filtering rounds not analyzed
Statistical rigor concerns: standard errors omitted 'for visibility'; no formal hypothesis testing or confidence intervals; win rate percentages lack statistical significance quantification
Limited generalization: main results on image classification only; audio use case restricted to single dataset (ESC50); no experiments on NLP, time series, or other domains

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing real practitioner challenge of AL strategy selection variability across datasets and models

Simple, training-free progressive filtering approach with solid theoretical justification (three theorems with correct proofs on value preservation, exponential reduction of uninformative instances, and monotonic value concentration)
Comprehensive experimental validation: 6 datasets, 3 foundation models, 8 baseline strategies, 4 ensemble methods, extensive ablations, and use case study demonstrating practical utility
Consistent performance improvements: 85% win rate vs BAIT, 80% vs UHerding, 100% vs SelectAL/TAILOR; REFINE outperforms all baselines across nearly every dataset-model combination
Valuable independent contribution: progressive filtering as preprocessing improves any AL strategy (+0.7% to +5.4%), with particular benefit for weak strategies, demonstrated on audio use case
Thorough supplementary material with detailed proofs, numerical examples, robustness tests (class imbalance, distribution shift, fine-tuning), parallel timing analysis, and complete learning curves
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: core contribution (iteratively taking unions of strategy selections) is conceptually straightforward and incremental; essentially combining existing filtering and ensembling ideas
Hyperparameter selection lacks principled methodology: α=0.4, R=5, J=10 set via CIFAR-10 only with no generalizable guidance for new domains; Table 2b shows non-negligible variance across α values

Ensemble composition not systematically studied: all available strategies included without justification; Figure 10 shows performance collapse with weak majority but cause-and-effect unclear; recommendation to use 'well-established complementary strategies' is vague

Critical failure mode underexplored: Dopanim/CLIP degradation and sensitivity to weak ensemble members acknowledged but relegated to appendix; practitioners cannot easily detect these scenarios in advance

Computational overhead inadequately addressed: Table 3 shows 10:31 min acquisition at cycle 20 (comparable to training); modest 5-10% improvements may not justify 2-3× cost; only one AutoAL timing comparison provided

Theoretical limitations: Theorem 3 assumes all strategies prefer high-value instances (may not hold for biased strategies); Definition 1 (ϵ-uninformative) somewhat circular; bounds are loose with limited convergence analysis
Second-stage selection not novel: coverage-based UHerding is existing AL strategy; contribution primarily Stage 1; Figure 11 suggests Stage 2 may be less critical than claimed

Insufficient guidance on practical applicability: no principled cost-benefit analysis, no clear scenarios where REFINE outweighs computational overhead vs simpler alternatives, limited analysis of when single strong strategy suffices
Statistical significance not emphasized in main paper: Friedman tests mentioned only in Appendix E; some learning curves show overlapping error bars and modest improvements
Pool reduction aggressiveness not analyzed: Table 4 shows |C_R|/|U| from 5% to 47% across datasets with no analysis of whether more aggressive filtering is beneficial or harmful
